## Proposed change
<!--
  Describe the big picture of your changes here to communicate to the
  maintainers why we should accept this pull request. If it fixes a bug
  or resolves a feature request, be sure to link to that issue in the
  additional information section.
-->
Implement Reolink ONVIF long polling as backup for the existing ONVIF WS base notification.
New order of receiving motion/AI detection events:
1) ONVIF ws base notification (delay <0.3 seconds)
2) ONVIF pull point long polling (delay +- 0.6 second)
3) Fast polling over HTTP (intervall = 5 seconds)

If 1 works, 2 and 3 will not be happening, if 2 works 3 will not be happening.

1) is the best option since it gives the fastest responses and is the least resource intensive, but unfortentely does not work in all siturations due to network configuration issues (requires HTTP, not compatible with SSL (HTTPS), does not always work accros VLANS if acces is not properly configured, requires proper configuration of the HomeAssistant internal URL adress).

Recommended by @bdraco here: https://github.com/home-assistant/core/pull/92837#discussion_r1188540016

~Requires reolink-aio bump to 0.7.0 from this PR first: https://github.com/home-assistant/core/pull/94761~
~Bringing test coverage back to 100% has been split out to this PR: https://github.com/home-assistant/core/pull/94763
Preferably that will be merged first.~

issue_context.title: Reolink doorbell ONVIF pushes no longer being received in 2023.4.6
issue_context.body:
### The problem

I was having issues with doorbell events (specifically the "visitor" state, though I didn't do much testing of the others) as described in #91030. When I upgraded to 2023.4.5, which included the fix, my issues mostly went away -- doorbell presses were occasionally delayed, but seemed to reliably show up. Since upgrading to 2023.4.6, I haven't been able to receive any doorbell press events at all. I tried rebooting the camera, deleting and re-adding the integration, and restarting home assistant. None of these things seemed to help. After my latest reboot, I haven't seen the "failed to call webhook" warning, so I believe that the onvif callback is indeed registering.

Debug logging is turned on for reolink, and  I've attached my logs in case they help.

Thank you so much for your work on this integration!


### What version of Home Assistant Core has the issue?

core-2023.4.6

### What was the last working version of Home Assistant Core?

core-2023.4.5

### What type of installation are you running?

Home Assistant Container

### Integration causing the issue

reolink

### Link to integration documentation on our website

https://www.home-assistant.io/integrations/reolink

### Diagnostics information

[home-assistant_2023-04-26T04-52-20.904Z.log](https://github.com/home-assistant/core/files/11329147/home-assistant_2023-04-26T04-52-20.904Z.log)

### Example YAML snippet

_No response_

### Anything in the logs that might be useful for us?

_No response_

### Additional information

_No response_

review_comments: If they already switched to long polling should we still try to renew the webhook?  It seems like its unlikely to start working later

Yes, there are some models like the older hardware versions of the E1 Zoom that do not publish the initial state upon subscription to the ONVIF WS base notification. For those models there is no way of knowing the subscription is working or not until the cam detect motion for the first time and a event comes in. Some users have reported that this sometimes takes many hours before someone walks past a camera....

In those cases we should use the ONVIF long polling to make sure we do receive events and it will automatically stop long polling as soon as WS base subscription kicks in and is confirmed to work.
So we can stop the renew as soon as we get a webhook?
Maybe store that in the config entry data so we reduce the load on the camera?

Yes that is already implemented: when a webhook is received, self._webhook_reachable becomes True, inside _async_long_polling the long polling will be stopped and self._long_poll_task becomes None. Therefore the long polling subscription will not be renewed anymore.

Storing in the config entry data is definitely possible, but it does add quite some complexity and I think it will result in more issues than it is going to resolve.
(Users might get stuck on long polling if the webhook subscription does not work for one time while they change network settings for instance).
Are there cameras that don't support pull point?  Ideally we can get rid of the complexity of having 3 methods to get the events

Yes there are some old camera models that do not support ONVIF at all but do support the HTTP API polling.
Therefore I would like to stick with this 3 fold approach.
Note to self: Need to check this line when I'm back at my desk

with onvif we sleep 0.75 seconds between polls to give a bit of a cooldown when the camera returns no events since sometimes the firmware gets stuck on some cameras and we end up polling in a loop and using all the cpu time otherwise
